sources.entry: VP Engineering vs CTO - Fred Wilson *(Union Square Ventures)*

summary.title: VP Engineering Vs CTO
summary.one_liner: The VP Engineering role centers on management and team building, while the CTO is the strongest technologist focused on architecture and technical direction, and the two are often peers rather than strictly senior and junior.
keywords: difference between vp engineering and cto
when to split cto and vp engineering
can one person be cto and vp eng
takeaways: A VP Engineering is ideally a strong manager, team builder, recruiter and issue resolver focused on making the engineering organization successful.
A CTO is ideally the strongest technologist, acting as architect and thinker, and is often the technical co-founder.
VP Engineering and CTO are often peers, and either can report to the other, though a VP Eng reporting to a CTO is more common.
Early startups typically have neither role; a technical co-founder often covers both until the engineering team needs a management layer.
It is very rare for one person to do both jobs well because they require different skills and time allocations.
summary.summary: Fred Wilson's short AVC post, part of his MBA Mondays series, explains how the VP Engineering and CTO roles differ, arguing that seniority is often not the main distinction. He describes the ideal VP Eng as a manager and team builder and the ideal CTO as the strongest technologist, then walks through how the roles typically emerge as a startup grows. The comment thread adds practitioner views on when to split the roles (often around 20 people), CTO and CIO differences, and the rarity of people who can do both.
